problem.text: Let $N = 123456789101112\dots4344$ be the $79$-digit number that is formed by writing the integers from $1$ to $44$ in order, one after the other. What is the remainder when $N$ is divided by $45$?

steps.title: Where to start: split $45$ into $5$ and $9$
steps.body: Dividing a $79$-digit number by $45$ directly is hopeless. But $45 = 5\cdot 9$, and $5$ and $9$ share no common factor, so by the Chinese Remainder Theorem the remainder mod $45$ is fixed once we know the remainders mod $5$ and mod $9$. Both of those have easy divisibility rules that only look at digits.

your_turn.prompt: Why would splitting $45$ as $3\cdot 15$ not work the same way?
your_turn.answer: $3$ and $15$ share the factor $3$. The two moduli must be relatively prime.

steps.title: The remainder mod $5$
steps.body: For division by $5$ only the units digit matters. The number $N$ ends with $\dots 4344$, so its last digit is $4$, and $N \equiv 4 \pmod 5$.

your_turn.prompt: Why does only the last digit matter when dividing by $5$?
your_turn.answer: Everything except the units digit is a multiple of $10$, which is a multiple of $5$.

steps.title: The remainder mod $9$
steps.body:
Since $10 \equiv 1 \pmod 9$, every power of $10$ is $\equiv 1 \pmod 9$. So each block of $N$ counts as just its own value: $N = 1\cdot 10^{78} + 2\cdot 10^{77} + \dots + 43\cdot 10^{2} + 44$ gives
$$N \equiv 1 + 2 + 3 + \dots + 44 \pmod 9$$
Careful: $1 + 2 + \dots + 44$ is not the digit sum of $N$, but the two leave the same remainder mod $9$, and that is all we need.

your_turn.prompt: Compute $1 + 2 + \dots + 44$ and its remainder when divided by $9$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: We need a remainder $r$ from $0$ to $44$ with $r \equiv 0 \pmod 9$ and $r \equiv 4 \pmod 5$. The multiples of $9$ in that range are $0, 9, 18, 27, 36$, which leave remainders $0, 4, 3, 2, 1$ when divided by $5$. Only $9$ works, so $N \equiv 9 \pmod{45}$. The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.B: This is only the remainder mod $5$ (the last digit $4$). The remainder mod $45$ must also be a multiple of $9$, and $4$ is not.
